raw.assessment: The incumbent provides a predictable conversational routine and printed access; seven frequent attendees explicitly valued its repeated structure (H3-O6). Its benefit is nevertheless uneven: five occasional attendees struggled to enter a conversation familiar to their partner, a concrete limitation on assuming predictability makes participation easy for everyone. Familiarity causing that difficulty remains a hypothesis. Success is unestablished: useful practice was reported on 49/72 returned slips, correct preparation on 48/72, and coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Missing slips, untimed speaking and unlinked responses limit inference.

openings.claim: A brief mutual introduction to each prompt, followed by equal speaking turns, may make the existing routine easier to enter without prior attendance or public proficiency labels.
openings.delta: Preserve the familiar session sequence but print a self-contained entry prompt and turn instructions on existing sheets; reserve their time within the 75 minutes.
openings.prediction: If conversational entry and unequal turns limit practice, entry difficulty and within-pair speaking imbalance should decrease even when pair-formation time stays similar. Improvement only in pairing time would not support this account.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary and entry-supported rounds, reversing order in another session. Observe anonymous speaking durations and partner changes; collect round-specific usefulness and entry-difficulty responses. Include planning and printing in weekly coordination totals.
assumptions: Participants accept turn instructions and can use the entry prompts.
Observation fits existing volunteer time; otherwise restrict the sampled pairs.
More balanced speaking need not be more useful and must be checked separately.

openings.claim: Confusion between current and earlier preparation tasks may contribute to incorrect task identification; a dated next-session box could reduce that confusion.
openings.delta: Add one clearly dated preparation instruction to each existing paper sheet, retaining optional messaging and allowing preparation-free participation.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers should fall when the dated box is present; unchanged errors despite correct on-sheet lookup would favor recall or instruction-comprehension problems over document ambiguity.
openings.probe: Compare ordinary and boxed sheets across sessions using anonymous unaided task identification followed by on-sheet lookup. Record blank and earlier-task answers separately, paper-only access, total weekly coordination time and conversational usefulness.
assumptions: The next task can be fixed before printing.
Adding the box requires little recurring volunteer effort.
Unaided identification and lookup are measured consistently.

raw.assessment: The observations identify entry, preparation and coordination difficulties but do not establish their causes. These are interaction hypotheses; neither is demonstrated to meet the six-session targets.

openings.claim: Cross a shared, self-contained opening prompt with privately selected prompt scaffolds at the first paired exchange. Everyone starts a fresh conversation; each speaker can use printed sentence starters or optional follow-up challenges without declaring a proficiency label.
openings.delta: A fresh prompt alone may leave language demands mismatched; scaffolds alone may leave occasional attendees entering an established conversation. Their combination may make the shared starting point usable at different current levels.
openings.prediction: The combination increases useful speaking time and reduces early partner changes more than either component alone, especially for participants unfamiliar with the topic.
openings.probe: Within existing practice time, rotate comparable fresh prompts through baseline, restart-only, scaffold-only and combined exchanges, varying order. Anonymously observe speaking time and partner changes; collect usefulness ratings and topic familiarity. Compare the combined improvement with the sum of separate improvements; log preparation effort.
assumptions: Reusable scaffolds can be printed within available resources.
Participants may freely ignore scaffolds; no prior attendance is required.
Measured speaking time requires participant usefulness ratings to establish value.

openings.claim: Cross a dated, detachable next-session preparation card with a brief partner explanation at the preparation handoff. Each participant explains the card's task aloud, then checks their interpretation against its printed example; spare copies remain available for people missing a session.
openings.delta: Dating helps distinguish old tasks but cannot establish understanding. Explanation can reveal confusion but may rehearse an outdated task. Their interface may prevent both errors while adding conversational practice.
openings.prediction: Combined cards and explanation produce fewer earlier-task answers and blanks than either alone, with fewer subsequent clarification messages.
openings.probe: Compare ordinary handoffs, dated cards alone, explanation alone and both across comparable sessions. Record anonymous task identification, clarification-message counts and total volunteer minutes; retain the six-session thresholds as the adoption test.
assumptions: Cards are obtainable at an existing accessible paper pickup point between sessions.
The explanation replaces existing wrap-up time.
Task identification remains separate from useful-speaking assessment.

openings.claim: Self-contained entry prompts plus equal turns may ease conversational entry.
openings.discriminator: Less entry difficulty and speaking imbalance despite unchanged pairing time.
openings.probe: Alternate supported/ordinary rounds; reverse order; observe durations, partner changes, usefulness and entry difficulty; log coordination.
openings.uncertainty: Turn acceptance unknown; balance need not imply usefulness; sample pairs if observation exceeds capacity.

openings.claim: A dated preparation box may prevent old-task confusion.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors fall; correct lookup with persistent unaided errors favors recall/comprehension explanations.
openings.probe: Compare ordinary/boxed sheets: unaided identification then lookup; separate blanks/earlier answers; track paper access, coordination and usefulness.
openings.uncertainty: Requires next task fixed before printing and consistent measurement.

openings.claim: Fresh shared prompts and privately selected scaffolds may jointly address familiarity and language-demand mismatch.
openings.discriminator: Combined benefit exceeds summed separate improvements, especially for unfamiliar participants.
openings.fit: Optional printed scaffolds; no public level label.
openings.probe: Rotate baseline, restart, scaffold and combined exchanges with varied order; measure speaking, usefulness, familiarity, partner changes and preparation effort.
openings.uncertainty: Scaffolds must be reusable within resources; speaking duration alone is insufficient.

openings.claim: Dated detachable cards plus partner explanation and example-checking may jointly prevent outdated-task and comprehension errors.
openings.discriminator: Combination reduces earlier-task answers, blanks and clarification messages beyond either alone.
openings.fit: Replace wrap-up; retain accessible spare paper copies.
openings.probe: Compare four handoff conditions across comparable sessions; record task identification, messages and total volunteer minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Accessible between-session pickup is assumed; usefulness remains separately assessed.

post_distill.decision: Probe candidates; none proven by synthetic observations with missing, untimed, unlinked reports. All must remain free, inclusive of absence and label refusal, offline-accessible, conversational, within 75 minutes and unpaid resources. Adoption requires six-session targets: 80% useful speaking, 85% preparation identification, coordination below 90 minutes/week.
